items.summary: Now open to everyone: manage multiple coding agents in one app, switch to another agent inside the same task without losing context, and continue from your phone — follow progress and open generated work. Connect a Runner on each machine; 15 agents are available today, including Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity.
items.title: OpenTandem: one hub for many coding agents, switch agents mid-task from your phone

items.summary: Launched November 1: each agent gets its own email address, Slack handle and Telegram handle, all behind one API; message it from wherever you already work and it replies in the same thread, including approving or rejecting an agent action straight from Slack. Open source, and works with Claude, Grok, OpenAI and other agent frameworks.
items.title: Agent Inbox: give every agent its own email, Slack and Telegram identity behind one API

items.summary: Published October 31 under MIT as a research prototype: it listens to a single GitHub repository (optionally Feishu), and when an authorized member asks for work, a Router dispatches it to isolated Worker sessions with their own directories, which reply in the original conversation with results such as a pull request. DeepSeek states plainly that it is research code, not an official product and not production-ready.
items.title: DeepSeek dsh-superagent: a proactive coding agent that watches a repo and answers with pull requests
